field_matrix.field_split: Often less readily shattering; floret callus tends to be fractured/peg-like rather than the conspicuously hairy, naturally disarticulating wild-oat base. Awns can be reduced or less twisted; cultivated varieties vary.
field_matrix.critical_photo: Same-scale mature florets: hairy callus, natural scar, dorsal awn and intact glumes.
field_matrix.guardrail: Do not distinguish vegetative plants or an isolated panicle confidently; cultivated/feral intermediates exist.

field_matrix.field_split: Brome has smaller many-flowered spikelets and lemma awns emerging near the lemma tip, not the stout twisted dorsal oat awn; inspect awn attachment.
field_matrix.critical_photo: Dissected lemma with its awn origin and complete spikelet.

field_matrix.field_split: Compact unbranched bristly spike with three one-flowered spikelets per rachis node, versus a loose branched oat panicle bearing hanging multiflowered spikelets.
field_matrix.critical_photo: One attached barley rachis node showing its three spikelets.

field_matrix.field_split: Long unbranched cereal spike with spikelets attached along a main axis, rather than an open drooping panicle.

measured_confirmation.growth_form: Cool-season annual with fibrous roots, without creeping rhizomes or stolons; seedling leaf twist is a supporting clue, not a mature-species proof.
measured_confirmation.ligule: Membranous, usually 4–6 mm long; no auricles (Flora of North America treatment).
measured_confirmation.panicle: Open, usually nodding panicle about 7–40 cm long; photograph the full branching head rather than a single detached spikelet.
measured_confirmation.spikelet: Usually 2–3 fertile florets; mature spikelet about 18–32 mm long; each floret commonly breaks away separately above the persistent glumes.
measured_confirmation.glumes: Two subequal, papery, typically 18–32 mm long and 9–11-veined; record length without any lemma awn.
measured_confirmation.fertile_lemma: Usually 14–22 mm long, often hairy below midpoint, with a dorsal awn arising around the middle third; record its own apex and hairiness.
measured_confirmation.lemma_awn: Commonly 23–42 mm long, conspicuously knee-bent and twisted below the bend; distinguish awn attachment to lemma from glume tips.
measured_confirmation.callus: Hairy floret base and distinct rounded-to-triangular disarticulation scar; photograph from a naturally detached ripe floret at 10–20×.
measured_confirmation.identification_limit: Ranges are published species descriptions, NOT measurements taken from the existing project photograph. A. fatua and cultivated A. sativa can be indistinguishable without mature florets; leave Avena sp. if shattering, callus and awn are unresolved.

crew_photo_sequence: 1. Same rooted plant: annual fibrous crown, complete drooping open panicle, and a centimeter scale.
2. Open blade/sheath collar with 1-mm scale to document the actual 4–6 mm membranous ligule and absent auricles.
3. Intact mature spikelet in side view beside millimeter ruler, showing both 18–32 mm glumes and number of florets.
4. One mature detached floret: lemma and dorsal bent/twisted awn photographed separately, with attachment point in focus.
5. 10–20× callus and natural disarticulation scar showing basal hairs; paired A. sativa comparison with equivalent scale and provenance.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — DANGLING OAT SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Loose, nodding branched panicle with large hanging 2–3-flowered spikelets; not a barley or rye spike.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Begin with the TWO archived Texas in-situ Avena fatua photos (panels 4–5): trace each open, often nodding, branched panicle to the pendent spikelets. Panel 0 adds an older source-identified flowering view. None exposes connected roots or proves the mature floret callus. A 7–40 cm panicle and 2–3-flowered large spikelets are published traits, not independently measured from these photographs. Contrast the unbranched spikes of Hordeum and Secale.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL TEXAS HABIT PHOTOS — RIPE FLORET STILL REQUIRED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTS AND TRUE LEAF COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Cool-season fibrous-rooted annual; 4–6 mm acute membranous ligule; auricles absent.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 1 is a physically archived Matt Lavin true INNER membranous ligule at the blade–sheath junction; its nearby finger is not a millimeter ruler. The 4–6 mm membrane and lack of auricles are published descriptions, not demonstrated measurements. A same-plant Texas rooted crown, opened collar and millimeter scale remain needed.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL INNER LIGULE PHOTO — CALIBRATED TEXAS SAME-PLANT VIEW MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · TWO LARGE GLUMES ENCLOSE THE FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Mature spikelet 18–32 mm; 2(–3) florets; two subequal 18–32 mm, usually 9–11-veined glumes.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 2 is a physically archived opened A. fatua spikelet with actual papery outer glumes, inner florets and stout awn. At 10–20× measure one ripe 18–32 mm spikelet and two separately exposed 18–32 mm, commonly 9–11-veined glumes; count 2–3 florets inside ONE spikelet. The photograph is not calibrated and does not prove those vein counts. Published measurements are not pixel measurements.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PARTIAL MACRO — SEPARATED MEASURED GLUMES MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · HAIRY LEMMA, DORSAL BENT AWN AND CALLUS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma 14–22 mm; dorsal twisted/knee-bent awn 23–42 mm, inserted near lemma middle third.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 3 is a physically archived Matt Lavin detached floret with genuine basal hairs and a twisted, knee-bent awn. Published fertile lemma length is about 14–22 mm and awn about 23–42 mm, dorsally inserted near the middle third; the gallery cannot yet measure or independently pinpoint that attachment or a natural shattering scar. Photograph the ripe detached floret at 10–20× with a ruler and a clear callus/rachilla scar.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL MACRO — AWN ORIGIN/CALLUS SCAR NEED SCALE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Cultivated oat can mimic wild oat; Japanese brome has tip-origin lemma awns.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panels 6 and 7 are EXPLICITLY OTHER-SPECIES photographs: Avena barbata (slender oat) spikelet and cultivated A. sativa whole plant. Panels 2–3 are genuine A. fatua anatomy. Compare same-stage ripe spikelets, awn insertion, callus hairs and natural disarticulation; A. sativa and A. fatua can overlap, and A. barbata must not be mislabeled wild oat. Bromus japonicus has smaller many-flowered spikelets with near-tip lemma awns; Hordeum and Secale bear unbranched spikes. If ripe floret characters remain unresolved, record Avena sp.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL TWO-SPECIES COMPARISONS — MATCHED RIPE FLORETS STILL NEEDED
